title: Statins and LDL cholesterol
markdown:
## In plain English
Randomized trials show that lowering LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) reduces major cardiovascular events. More intensive LDL-C lowering (target <55 mg/dL) reduced events versus a conventional target (<70 mg/dL) in a recent randomized trial, and large trials of nonstatin LDL-C–lowering drugs that further reduce LDL-C on top of statins also lowered cardiovascular events. Other trials show substantial LDL-C lowering with new agents (PCSK9 inhibitors, inclisiran) though not all had clinical-outcome data in these abstracts. [PMID 41910315](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41910315/) [PMID 28304224](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28304224/) [PMID 36876740](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36876740/) [PMID 32187462](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32187462/)

## Key findings
- A randomized trial of patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease found that targeting LDL-C <55 mg/dL vs <70 mg/dL (median achieved 56 vs 66 mg/dL) reduced the 3-year composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina (hazard ratio 0.67). Safety end points were similar between groups in that trial. [PMID 41910315](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41910315/)
- In a large randomized, placebo-controlled trial (27,564 patients on statins), the PCSK9 inhibitor evolocumab lowered LDL-C by ~59% (median baseline 92 mg/dL to 30 mg/dL) and significantly reduced the composite of cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, unstable-angina hospitalization, or revascularization (HR 0.85) and the key composite of cardiovascular death/MI/stroke (HR 0.80). Results were consistent across subgroups. [PMID 28304224](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28304224/)
- In statin-intolerant patients, the ATP-citrate lyase inhibitor bempedoic acid reduced LDL-C (mean baseline ~139 mg/dL; absolute reduction ~29.2 mg/dL at 6 months) and reduced the primary composite cardiovascular outcome over median 40.6 months (HR 0.87). [PMID 36876740](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36876740/)
- Inclisiran, an siRNA that lowers hepatic PCSK9 production, produced sustained ~50% reductions in LDL-C with dosing every 6 months in two phase 3 trials; those abstracts report lipid reductions and safety but not clinical-outcome results. [PMID 32187462](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32187462/)
- Reviews summarize that statins are the mainstay for lowering LDL-C and preventing cardiovascular disease, discuss statin adverse effects (especially muscle symptoms), and describe newer nonstatin LDL-C–lowering therapies (PCSK9 inhibitors, inclisiran, bempedoic acid) as alternatives or additions. These reviews discuss mechanisms and clinical considerations but are narrative (not pooled outcome trials). [PMID 37956957](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37956957/) [PMID 30653440](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30653440/) [PMID 28057795](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28057795/) [PMID 37567512](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37567512/)

## How strong is the evidence?
The strongest evidence in these abstracts comes from randomized controlled trials, including one large outcomes trial of a PCSK9 inhibitor (n=27,564) and other randomized outcome trials (the intensive-target LDL trial with 3,048 patients and the bempedoic acid trial with ~13,970 patients). These are randomized clinical trials measuring hard cardiovascular endpoints, which provides high-quality evidence that additional LDL-C lowering reduces events in secondary-prevention populations. Some abstracts (inclisiran trials) report large, well-conducted phase 3 randomized trials for LDL-C lowering but did not report clinical-outcome results in the provided abstracts.

## Limitations and caveats
- These abstracts primarily address patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or high risk; they do not directly report effects in all primary-prevention groups.
- Not every LDL-C–lowering agent in these abstracts reported clinical-outcome results here (inclisiran abstracts report lipid changes; outcome effects are not included in those abstracts). [PMID 32187462](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32187462/)
- Narrative reviews describe mechanisms, pleiotropic effects, and adverse effects but do not provide pooled or randomized-outcome evidence; they summarize background and hypotheses rather than proving causal effects. [PMID 28057795](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28057795/) [PMID 30653440](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30653440/) [PMID 37567512](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37567512/)
- These abstracts do not provide individual-patient guidance, long-term noncardiovascular safety beyond trial duration, or comparisons of all possible LDL-C targets across diverse populations.

## Sources
Based on 8 PubMed abstracts: 4 randomized controlled trials, 4 narrative reviews. Abstracts only, not full papers. Includes clinical trials, but no pooled analysis.

1. Intensive LDL Cholesterol Targeting in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease. *The New England journal of medicine, 2026* · Randomized controlled trial · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41910315/)
2. Evolocumab and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Cardiovascular Disease. *The New England journal of medicine, 2017* · Randomized controlled trial · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28304224/)
3. Bempedoic Acid and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Statin-Intolerant Patients. *The New England journal of medicine, 2023* · Randomized controlled trial · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36876740/)
4. Two Phase 3 Trials of Inclisiran in Patients with Elevated LDL Cholesterol. *The New England journal of medicine, 2020* · Randomized controlled trial · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32187462/)
5. Dyslipidemia in diabetes. *Indian heart journal, 2024* · Narrative review · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37956957/)
6. Statin Toxicity. *Circulation research, 2019* · Narrative review · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30653440/)
7. Pleiotropic Effects of Statins on the Cardiovascular System. *Circulation research, 2017* · Narrative review · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28057795/)
8. Beyond statins: New pharmacological targets to decrease LDL-cholesterol and cardiovascular events. *Pharmacology & therapeutics, 2023* · Narrative review · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37567512/)
